newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Ex-communist wins Mongolia president poll - party.
newsitem.headline: Ex-communist wins Mongolia president poll - party.

text.p: The candidate of Mongolia's ex-communist opposition People's Revolutionary Party (MPRP) has won an election for a new president, beating the incumbent who stood with government backing, party officials said on Monday.
"(Natsagiin) Bagabandi has won the elections," said a spokesman for the MPRP.
The spokesman said Bagabandi, 47, had won in 115 constituencies out of 119 with overall support of more than 60 percent with almost all votes counted.

The presidential polls, only the second direct election in Mongolia, saw the defeat of incumbent President Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat, the candidate of the ruling Democratic Union Coalition, party officials conceded.
A coalition spokesman said Ochirbat was believed to have garnered about 30 percent of the vote.
Election committee officials said election turnout was estimated at about 78.2 percent of the 1.1 million eligible votes in the sprawling land of the steppes.
